messages.subject: Tractography Matrices - Normalize by size - size.txt
parts:
Hi Chris,

I would like to normalize my DTI data by size of ROIs (I assume this means the volumes of each region?). I have imported my DTI data from elsewhere using Freesurfer surfaces as inputs for defining ROIs so I would like to use the Freesurferr volume estimates. However, without an example size.txt file from the user guide, I am not entirely sure in what format/layout I should have this file in. How should I format this text file?


This is the case for many of the files if you have used a software package other than that used by the userguide. Maybe a folder on the github page containing these files for a 'worked example' would be useful for people to run through an example but also compare outputs/inputs?

BW
Dan

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Tractography Matrices - Normalize by size - size.txt
parts:
Hi Dan, the format of the file should be a single column in which each row of the file is the volume of each region. The order should match that of "waytotal" and the rows of "fdt_network_matrix" (or whatever connectivity matrix you generate with other software).

I will certainly add some more information to the User Guide. It is sometimes difficult for me to "think like a beginner" in terms of what is unclear in the User Guide and package docs, since I know the package so well. In terms of putting worked examples on Github, I doubt I will be able to add it to the package itself, but other packages have a separate "data" package (for example, there is the "igraphdata" package) that separates the example datasets from the package itself. That is a solution I will look into, but not for this next release. In the meantime, I will be more clear in the User Guide.

Chris

Don't apologize for questions, they help me learn what aspects of the package are stumbling blocks for other users!

What were the arguments you supplied to "create_mats"? "A.bin" and "A.bin.sums" are going to be non-NULL only if "threshold.by='consensus'" so it might not be a problem.

It looks like you only have 1 group, and the code creating "g.group", "g.norm", "fnames" is *supposed* to create an empty (NULL) list of length equal to #groups.

1) A.norm.sub <- my.mats$A.norm.sub
2) Change your script to use "my.mats$A.norm.sub" anywhere you see that object

Chris
